1. Preparing Before Mantra Recitation

Choose a clean, quiet place; dress neatly and sit or stand upright. Join your palms, steady your breathing, and direct sincere reverence toward the Medicine Buddha. If lighting a lamp or offering incense, ensure safety.

2. Choosing a Suitable Way to Practice

When you have sufficient time, open the “Recitation Ritual” section and follow the entire ritual in order: opening homage, purification mantras, incense offering, prayer, prostrations to the Buddhas, making vows, reciting the mantra, dedication of merit, and taking the Three Refuges.

When time is limited, you may observe a short session reciting the Medicine Buddha Mantra. Go directly to the section “MEDICINE BUDDHA ABHIṢEKA MANTRA” in the text, recite for your chosen number of repetitions, and conclude by reciting the Buddha’s sacred name and dedicating merit.

3. Setting Your Intention and Vow

Before chanting, incline your mind toward goodness, resolve to mend unwholesome habits, and pray for peace for yourself and those to whom you dedicate merit. When following the full ritual, recite the prayer and vows in the text, silently inserting the name and Dharma name of the person being prayed for at the blank spaces.

4. Reciting and Counting Repetitions

Depending on your time and circumstances, choose 3, 7, 21, 49, or 108 repetitions. Chant clearly and evenly without rushing for numbers. One complete recitation from “Nam mo Bac gia phat de” through “tam mot yet de toa ha” counts as one repetition.

You may use prayer beads or the counter in practice mode, recording each count only after completing the entire mantra. Whenever your mind wanders, gently bring attention back to the words.

5. Reciting the Sacred Name Afterward

After the mantra section, recite “Namo Medicine Master Beryl Radiance King Buddha” 21 times as printed in the ritual. If performing the full liturgy, continue through the Untying Karmic Knots verse, the Heart Sutra, and Buddha-mindfulness in sequence.

6. Merit Dedication and Conclusion

Recite the Merit Dedication verses followed by the Three Refuges at the end of the ritual. Maintain a reverent heart, wishing well-being for yourself and all sentient beings, and practice steadily according to your capacity.

Namo Fundamental Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha

Namo Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Medicine Buddha Assembly

RECITATION RITUAL

INCENSE CONTEMPLATION

(After lighting the lamp and incense, stand upright with palms joined at chest level and silently recite)

PURIFICATION OF THE DHARMA REALM MANTRA

An lam xoa ha. (3 times)

PURIFICATION OF THE THREE KARMAS MANTRA

An ta pha ba pha, truat da ta pha dat ma ta pha, ba pha thuat do ham. (3 times)

(The officiant lights incense, kneels upright holding the incense at forehead level, and recites the Incense Offering verse).

INCENSE OFFERING & PRAISE OF THE BUDDHA

May this fragrant cloud of incense
Pervade the realms of the ten directions,
As an offering to all Buddhas,
The honored Dharma, all Bodhisattvas,
The countless assembly of Śrāvakas,
And all Worthies and Sages.
Giving rise to a radiant lotus dais
That extends throughout boundless worlds,
Perfuming all sentient beings
So all awaken the Bodhi mind,
Part from deluded karmic actions,
And fulfill the Unsurpassed Path.

(Bow three times, then recite the Prayer)

PRAYER

At this time, we your disciples recite these sutras and mantras, praise Your sacred names, and gather this merit. We beseech the ever-abiding Three Jewels of the ten directions, our Fundamental Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha, Medicine Master Beryl Radiance King Buddha, and all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Great Compassion Assembly to radiate compassionate light upon _______(silently state the name of the person)__, Dharma name _____________, so that the three poisons of greed, anger, and delusion may cease, karmic obstacles be purified, auspiciousness always be attained, the body be free from illness, the mind be free from affliction, peace and ease prevail at all times, all adverse conditions dissolve, and the Bodhisattva path be practiced life after life.

(Stand up, place the incense in the censer, stand upright with palms joined, and recite)

PRAISE OF THE BUDDHA

Unsurpassed King of the Dharma,
Without equal in the three realms,
Teacher of gods and humans,
Compassionate father of the four kinds of birth.
With one wholehearted thought of refuge,
The karma of three incalculable eons is purified;
We praise and extol Your virtues
Through countless unending ages.

CONTEMPLATION

Buddha and sentient beings have a nature ever empty and still;
Their spiritual communion is beyond conception.
Like Indra’s jeweled net is this place of practice:
All Buddhas of the ten directions shine brightly within.
Before the precious seat, our forms appear;
Bowing our heads, we vow to take refuge.

Wholeheartedly paying homage: Namo the ever-abiding Three Jewels—all Buddhas, the honored Dharma, and the noble Saṅgha pervading all space and the Dharma Realm throughout past, present, and future. (1 prostration)

Wholeheartedly paying homage: Namo Śākyamuni Buddha, Teacher of this Sahā world; Maitreya Buddha of the future Dragon-Flower assembly; Great-Wisdom Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva; Great-Conduct Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; Dharma-Protecting Bodhisattvas; and all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Vulture Peak Assembly. (1 prostration)

Wholeheartedly paying homage: Namo Amitābha Buddha, Greatly Compassionate Guide of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss; Namo Medicine Master Beryl Radiance King Buddha, Sovereign of the Eastern World Who Dispels Calamities and Prolongs Life; Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva; Great-Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva; and the Pure Great Ocean Assembly of Bodhisattvas. (1 prostration)

WILLOW-BRANCH PURE WATER PRAISE

Pure water from the wondrous willow branch
Sprinkles and quenches myriad sufferings.
Celestial beings are refreshed and pure in mind;
Humankind rejoices in serene peace.
Sweet nectar showers across the mortal world,
Flames of anger cease, and golden lotuses bloom.
Namo Cool Refreshing Ground Bodhisattva Mahāsattva. (3 times)

GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA

Namo Bodhisattvas of the Great Compassion Assembly. (3 times) Thousand-Hand Thousand-Eye Unobstructed Great Compassion Mind Dhāraṇī. Nam mo hac ra dat na, da ra da da. Nam mo a ri da, ba lo Yet de, thuoc bat ra da, bo de tat doa ba da, Ma ha tat doa ba da, ma ha ca lo ni ca da.

An tat ban ra phat due, so dat na dat toa. Nam mo tat kiet lat doa, y mong a ri da ba lo kiet de, that Phat ra lang da ba. Nam mo na ra can tri he ri, ma ha ban da sa me, tat ba a tha dau du bang, a the dung, tat ba tat da, na ma ba da, ma phat dac dau, dat diet tha.

An a ba lo he, lo ca de, ca ra de, di he ri, ma ha bo de tat doa, tat ba tat ba, ma ra ma ra, ma he ma he, ri da dung, cu lo cu lo kiet mong, do lo do lo phat xa da de, ma ha phat xa da de, da la da la, dia ri ni, that Phat ra da, da ra da ra.

Ma ma phat ma ra, muc de le, y he y he, that na that na, a ra sam Phat ra xa loi, phat sa phat sam, Phat ra xa da, ho lo ho lo ma ra, ho lo ho lo he ri, ta ra ta ra, tat ri tat ri, to ro to ro, bo de da, bo de da, bo da da, bo da da, di de ri da, na ra can tri, dia ri sat ni na, ba da ma na ta ba ha, tat da da ta ba ha.

Ma ha tat da da ta ba ha. Tat da du nghe that ban ra da ta ba ha. Na ra can tri ta ba ha. Ma ra na ra ta ba ha. Tat ra tang a muc khu gia, ta ba ha. Ta ba ma ha, a tat da da ta ba ha. Gia kiet ra a tat da da ta ba ha. Ba da ma kiet tat da da ta ba ha.

Na ra can tri ban da ra da ta ba ha. Ma ba ri thang kiet ra da, ta ba ha. Nam mo hac ra dat na da ra da da. Nam mo a ri da ba lo Yet de thuoc ban ra da, ta ba ha. An tat dien do man da ra bat da da ta ba ha. (3 times)

ASPIRATION FOR PRACTICE

I bow to the Honored One of the Three Realms
And take refuge in the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Now I make this vast vow
To recite the Medicine Buddha Mantra:
Above, to repay the four heavy debts;
Below, to relieve suffering in the three lower realms.
May all who see or hear of this
Awaken the Bodhi mind,
And at the end of this karmic life
Be reborn together in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Namo Fundamental Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha. (3 times)

SUTRA OPENING VERSE

The unsurpassed, profound, and subtle Dharma
Is rarely encountered even in millions of eons.
Now that I see, hear, and uphold it,
May I understand the Tathāgata’s true meaning.

Namo Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Medicine Buddha Assembly. (3 times)

Sovereign Teacher of the Eastern World,
Twelve great vows far proclaimed,
Delivering countless beings from suffering,
Revealing the true and eternal Dharma.
For forty-nine days with lamps and incense,
Adorning the entire sacred sanctuary,
Reciting His name and paying homage
Dispels calamities and grants longevity.

Fragile indeed is this Sahā world;
To benefit all beings, this Dharma was spoken.
The Seven Medicine Buddhas eradicate offenses;
Their Twelve Great Vows save all living beings.
Three thousand emanation Buddhas bless together;
Eight Bodhisattvas witness our sincere devotion.
Untying knots, averting harm, lengthening life,
Bringing auspicious blessings and peaceful well-being.

(Depending on your time and circumstances, recite 3, 7, 21, 49, or 108 times)

MEDICINE BUDDHA ABHIṢEKA MANTRA

Nam mo Bac gia phat de, be sat xa lu ro, thich luu li, bat lat ba, hat ra xa gia, dat tha yet da gia, a ra hat de, tam mieu tam bot da gia, dat diet tha. An be sat the, be sat the, be sat xa, tam mot yet de toa ha.

Namo Medicine Master Beryl Radiance King Buddha (21 times)

Untie the knots, untie all karmic knots;
Let grudges of countless lives dissolve.
Wash clean the worldly heart, arouse sincerity,
And before the Buddha’s altar pray to release all bonds:
Medicine Buddha, Medicine Buddha,
Disaster-Dispelling Longevity-Granting Medicine Buddha,
Wish-Fulfilling Medicine Buddha. (3 times)

May the Twelve Great Yakṣa Generals,
Aiding the Buddha in spreading this Dharma,
Untie those five-colored knotted threads,
Granting fulfillment according to every vow,
Ending all enmity and granting lasting health and peace.

MAHĀ PRAJÑĀPĀRAMITĀ HEART SUTRA

When Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva was practicing the profound Perfection of Wisdom, he illuminated the five aggregates, saw they were all empty, and crossed beyond all suffering and distress. Śāriputra, form does not differ from emptiness; emptiness does not differ from form. Form itself is emptiness; emptiness itself is form. So too are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Śāriputra, all dharmas are marked by emptiness: neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, neither increasing nor decreasing.

Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects; no realm of eye through no realm of mind-consciousness; no ignorance and no ending of ignorance, up to no aging and death and no ending of aging and death; no suffering, origin, cessation, or path; no wisdom and no attainment, because there is nothing to attain.

Relying on the Perfection of Wisdom, the Bodhisattva has no hindrance in mind; having no hindrance, there is no fear; far beyond inverted dreamlike thoughts, one reaches Ultimate Nirvāṇa. All Buddhas of the three times, relying on the Perfection of Wisdom, attain Unsurpassed Complete Perfect Awakening.

Therefore know that the Perfection of Wisdom is the great spiritual mantra, the great luminous mantra, the unsurpassed mantra, the unequaled mantra, able to remove all suffering—true and not false. Thus is spoken the mantra of the Perfection of Wisdom: Yet de, Yet de, Ba La Yet de, Ba La Tang Yet de, Bo De Tat Ba Ha. (3 times)

BUDDHA-MINDFULNESS AND MERIT DEDICATION

PRAISE OF AMITĀBHA BUDDHA

Amitābha Buddha’s body is pure gold;
His noble marks shine with self-adorned splendor.
His white ūrṇā curl winds like five Mount Sumerus;
His clear blue eyes are vast as the four great oceans.
Within His radiance appear countless Buddhas,
And Bodhisattvas beyond number manifest therein.
Forty-eight vows deliver sentient beings;
Nine lotus grades carry all to liberation.

I take refuge and bow to Amitābha Buddha
In the Western World of Peaceful Bliss.
Now I vow to be reborn in that Pure Land;
I humbly pray Your Compassion receives me.

Namo Amitābha Buddha, Greatly Compassionate One of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Namo Amitābha Buddha (recite as time permits) Namo Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva (3 times) Namo Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva (3 times) Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva (3 times) Namo Pure Great Ocean Assembly of Bodhisattvas (3 times)

DEDICATION OF MERIT

Chanting the mantra and praying for peace brings supreme merit;
All boundless blessings are hereby dedicated.
May every sentient being throughout the Dharma Realm
Swiftly reach the Land of Infinite Light.

May the three obstructions cease and afflictions end;
May true, clear wisdom arise;
May every karmic offense be wiped away;
And may we practice the Bodhisattva path in every life.

May we be born in the Western Pure Land,
With the nine lotus grades as our parents.
When the lotus opens, may we behold the Buddha, realize Non-Arising,
And dwell with non-retrogressing Bodhisattvas as companions.

May this merit
Extend universally to all;
May we and all sentient beings
Together accomplish the Buddha Way.

THE THREE REFUGES

I take refuge in the Buddha, wishing all sentient beings may understand the Great Way and generate the unsurpassed Bodhi mind. (1 prostration) I take refuge in the Dharma, wishing all sentient beings may deeply penetrate the Sutra Treasury and gain wisdom vast as the ocean. (1 prostration) I take refuge in the Saṅgha, wishing all sentient beings may harmonize the great assembly without any hindrance. (1 prostration)

May this merit
Reach out everywhere to all,
So that disciples and all sentient beings
Together attain Buddhahood.

May this merit
Adorn the Buddhas’ Pure Land,
Repay the four heavy debts above,
And relieve suffering in the three lower realms below.
May all who see or hear this
Awaken the Bodhi mind,
And when this karmic body ends,
Be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Upon arriving there,
Fulfilling all great vows,
May World-Honored Amitābha
Bestow the prophecy of Buddhahood.
Namo Dharma-Protecting Bodhisattvas.
